payload.statement: Daane et al. report a dominant ENU mutant, nr21, with small adult fins and no statistically decreased body size; they mapped it to chromosome 15, found a nonsynonymous T200K change in a conserved domain of the L-type amino-acid transporter lat4a, and show by cis frameshift revertants that the effect is a gain of function. Zebrafish lacking lat4a have no fin phenotype.
payload.title: Source statement (full text): the zebrafish dominant mutant nr21 carries T200K in lat4a and acts by gain of function

payload.context: [species: Danio rerio; evidence_class: causal_intervention (as reported); source card: daane2021-pdf] [lof_gof] p.4: "The ability to revert the mutant phenotype by loss-of-function kcnh2a alleles in cis to lof indicates the mutant imparts a gain-of-function effect"; [lof_breakpoints] p.15: "identified a breakpoint upstream of the transcription start site of prrx1a (23.174 Mb in Zv11) and one between kcc4a and kcnh2a (24.075 Mb)"; [lof_ectopic] p.8: "As ectopic expression of kcnh2a is sufficient to drive fin overgrowth (Figure 3)"
limitations: Breakpoint positions are given to 0.001 Mb: the 24.075 Mb breakpoint is consistent with, not proof of, the position about 5.6 kb upstream of the ZFIN GRCz11 kcnh2a start (24,080,694).
lof^dt2 and its revertants are not maintained, per the methods.

payload.statement: The paper states that loss-of-function kcnh2a alleles in cis revert the longfin phenotype, so lof imparts a gain of function; long-read mapping found breakpoints at 23.174 Mb (upstream of prrx1a) and 24.075 Mb (between kcc4a and kcnh2a) in Zv11; and that ectopic kcnh2a expression is sufficient to drive fin overgrowth.
payload.title: Source statement (full text): longfin (lof) is a kcnh2a gain of function from cis-ectopic expression; an inversion breakpoint lies between kcc4a and kcnh2a

payload.context: [species: Danio rerio; evidence_class: genotype_phenotype (as reported); source card: daane2021-pdf] The phenocopy concerns relative fin proportions only. [fig4_title] p.7: "Intersection of bioelectric and Lat4a-mediated growth pathways is sufficient to phenocopy the evolved flying fish fin allometry"; [fig4_suppressor] p.7: "lat4a is a fin suppressor of overgrowth caused by increased potassium channel function"; [fig4_transhet] p.7: "the nr21/lof trans-heterozygotes exhibit elongated paired fins and a hypocercal caudal fin"; [fig4_phenocopy] p.8: "suggesting the interaction between these two genes is sufficient to phenocopy this key innovation and organismal bauplan of flying fishes"; [fig4_mechanism] p.8: "the mechanism of fin-specific suppression of lof by lat4a mutations is occurring downstream of bioelectric signaling signals"; [fig4_qrt] p.8: "kcnh2a expression does not vary significantly in pectoral or dorsal fins containing the nr21 mutation"
limitations: No flight, gliding or aerodynamic measurement in zebrafish appears in the text read.
The mechanism is not identified.
The zebrafish alleles are not the flying-fish variants.

payload.context: [species: Beloniformes (35 species); evidence_class: sequence_annotation; source card: daane2021-pdf] [cap_species] p.3: "35 different beloniform species, including two- and four-winged flying fishes, halfbeaks, sauries, and needlefishes"; [cap_coverage] p.3: "We obtained coverage from an average of 78.3% of the targeted genomic regions at an average 38.3-fold depth"; [f326l] p.7: "we detected a shared amino acid substitution in lat4a that is found across multiple lineages having enlarged pectoral fins"; [f326l_caveat] p.7: "we cannot exclude incomplete lineage sorting or introgression of ancestral F326L haplotypes specifically within gliding lineages"; [lat4a_phyloP] p.5: "Lat4a also has a phyloP acceleration p = 0.008 on the common ancestral node of flying fishes"; [sailfin] p.7: "only one flying fish species in our dataset lacks the convergent lat4a allele, the sailfin flying fish Parexocoetus brachypterus"
limitations: Targeted capture of conserved regions from pooled individuals, not whole genomes.
The authors cannot exclude incomplete lineage sorting or introgression.
No functional test of F326L is reported in the text read; F326L (natural) is a different residue from T200K (laboratory).
